description: August Kekulé was a German chemist who made a breakthrough discovery in 1884-1885 with his concept of the benzene ring. This paradigm-shifting concept proposed that six carbon atoms were arranged in a hexagonal structure with alternating single and double bonds. Through this structure, Kekulé provided scientific evidence that disproved previously held views on carbon-based molecules. As a result of Kekulé's findings, the scientific community made further progress in the area of organic chemistry
